look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check an annual coarse squash vine or bush with alternate often deeply 5–7-lobed rough leaves. At stem nodes inspect stiff hairs and their swollen pustulate bases; on a mature fruit look for a firm, five-ribbed stalk. The staged image shows a cultivated straightneck squash plant, flowers and lobed leaves, NOT a stem-hair macro or a measured fruiting stalk.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual cultivated or escaped squash; sprawling vines or compact bush cultivars, variable growth form.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Alternate broad rough blades, often 5–7-lobed; cultivars vary in lobing, markings and size.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Large yellow unisexual flowers, with male and female flowers borne separately on same plant; female flower has swollen inferior ovary.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Very variable pepo fruit among pumpkin, zucchini and summer squash cultivars; fruiting peduncle often hard, five-angled/ribbed and not or gradually expanded at fruit.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Rough annual stems with commonly persistent hairs on strong pustulate bases; tendrils and nodes help separate from unrelated broad-leaved crops.
